description.narrative: The Project will contribute to alleviating the burden of NCDs such as cancers, cardiovascular diseases and other allied health conditions for patients and create direct and indirect job opportunities, including for medical professionals. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that this investment will promote competitiveness in the healthcare (oncology and medical diagnostic) market by demonstrating the model of co-location, cross subsidization of treatment cost; entry into an underdeveloped and highly specialized healthcare market with a growing demand, and upskilling medical personnels in an underdeveloped specialty. This is expected to catalyze significant movement among other private healthcare providers in the market.

The proposed IFC investment is an A-loan of up to US$24.3 million equivalent Nigerian Naira (NGN) to NSIA Advanced Medical Services Limited (MedServe or the Company), to expand its medical diagnostic and cancer treatment services, which comprises the roll-out of 13 new diagnostics health centers, 3 oncology (cancer) centers and 3 catheterization (cardiology) labs, across 13 states in Nigeria (the Project). The Project is expected to be supported by the IDA20 Private Sector Window Local Currency Facility (IDA PSW LCF), as described in the Blended Finance Section.
